## c2badae666ad

**Reproduced teaching shortcut — canonical distractor omitted.** Audited
`generator.py` SHA-256
`cc2688b4eedf869760ef88956f0fc170a606768d4753b57dc24800d28cdab4e5`
without modifying it. Across 400 deterministic default draws (100 each for
None/easy/medium/hard), every grid used only colors 0, 1, 2, and 3; none included
the extra irrelevant color present in every labeled canonical input. Therefore
a rival that normalizes **all nonzero colors** and returns cells belonging to
exactly two shapes agrees with the intended three-color computation on all 400
generated inputs.

The retained canonical train-pair-0 counterexample contains distractor color 7,
passes the selected `self_check`, and is accepted by `arcpuzzles apply` as in the
generator domain. The canonical Racket rule (`95b31785aa4f`) returns a 3x3 cyan
pattern, while the all-nonzero rival returns a different 2x2 pattern. Full
source-bound evidence is
`checks/audit/c2badae666ad/counterexample.json`; generation census and rival
construction are in `checks/audit/c2badae666ad/probe.json`, and the supported
Racket receipt is `checks/audit/c2badae666ad/racket.json`.

The isolated audit preset also failed because this generator declares no
`strict_canonical_like`, `SEMANTIC_WITNESSES`, or `lesson_identifiable` contract,
and it has no selected task-local/frozen tests:
`checks/audit/c2badae666ad-combined/`. Suggested future repair: sample an
irrelevant non-1/2/3 distractor with canonical-like frequency and location,
declare the all-nonzero rival, and require every lesson to refute it. This audit
is findings-only; the source was left unchanged.
